## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding at or above the critical threshold; one Important checklist failure and one Important reviewer finding remain as notes)

The PR is ready to merge: every acceptance criterion is itemized and the checklist rejects nothing at the critical threshold, but two Important wording problems are worth fixing first.

Rule applied: rule 6 — findings and a checklist FAIL below the threshold remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. `src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py` line 84, in the new "Ambiguous Questions" section, tells the agent that a clarifying-question turn overrides the one-row rule "because a lookup's rows are already shown above the question". That reason does not hold in every case. The same prompt says at line 68 that "the values of a very large row may not be shown", and at line 131 that such a row "shows at most its column headers, without values". `_format.py` also hides introspection DataFrames and trims trailing blocks to a byte budget. So the agent is told the user has already seen lookup values in cases where the user has not. Criterion 5 asks for this reason almost word for word, so the wording comes from the issue; the instruction itself (state no result on the question turn) is what the criterion requires. (raised by 1/3 agents)
- VC-7: FAIL (important) — The _GENERIC_INPUT_PLACEHOLDERS comment asserts that agent/core/agent/agent.py emits these four ChatInputUpdateComponent placeholders when a turn finishes and that none carries content for the user. [src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:119]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The four strings are each emitted by agent.py (241 'Try again...', 336/499 'Ask a question...', 1098 'Ask a follow-up question...', 1168 'Continue the task or ask me something else...') and none carries user content. But agent.py:1075 also emits ChatInputUpdateComponent(placeholder='Try rephrasing or narrowing the question...') when the tool loop stops on consecutive argument failures (break at 1079, turn end). It is absent from _GENERIC_INPUT_PLACEHOLDERS (_format.py:124-131), so the comment's implied completeness (these are the placeholders emitted at turn finish, all filtered) is wrong: that placeholder could be surfaced as the answer instead of '(no answer)'. The claim that the set holds the four emitted placeholders is correct, but the set is not exhaustive.

  </details>

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `docs/external/managing-memory.md` lines 38 to 42 describe what the model does as if it were certain: "A question about revenue that the note reaches then gets a clarifying question unless…" (line 38), "it uses the reading that the pair's SQL uses" (line 40), and "…and then it asks" (line 42). The code only puts an instruction in the system prompt, and nothing enforces it, as criterion 7 says. Line 36 of the same section and the new paragraph in `getting-started.md` hedge correctly ("is instructed to", "is meant to"). (raised by 1/3 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: hedging the sentence changes no output, branch or covered set; docs/external/*.md is read by no .sh, .py, .yml or workflow consumer and is not loaded as agent instructions; it is a published user doc page -->
2. `docs/external/getting-started.md` line 82 says the agent asks when "the readings give different numbers" and "is told not to ask when … the readings give the same numbers". The prompt's test is different: it asks when the readings count different records, a different period or a different measure, "without first measuring the difference" (`default.py` line 80), and exempts only readings that count the same records, period and measure (line 83). Two readings that count different records but give the same total still get a question, while this page tells users they will not. `managing-memory.md` line 36 states the rule correctly. (raised by 1/3 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=not-held; evidence: rewording the sentence changes no output, branch or covered set; docs/external/*.md is read by no .sh, .py, .yml or workflow consumer and is not loaded as agent instructions; it is a published user doc page -->
3. Test comments name the issue instead of the behavior they protect: the section banner "clarifying questions (issue #298)" at `tests/unit/test_server.py` line 593, and the docstring of `test_ambiguous_questions_section_always_present` in `tests/unit/test_system_prompt.py`, which begins "Issue #298: …". The rest of both comments is accurate. (raised by 1/3 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: test comments change no output, branch or covered set; no tool reads them for behavior; test files are not published -->

</details>
